requirements.quote:
FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR (0x03):  The endpoint detected that its peer
      violated the flow-control protocol.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint detects that its peer violated the flow-control protocol.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR error code, whose value is 0x03.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's error-code selection and numeric encoding can be checked for a detected flow-control violation.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_TIMEOUT (0x04):  The endpoint sent a SETTINGS frame but did
      not receive a response in a timely manner.  See Section 6.5.3
      ("Settings Synchronization").
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sent a SETTINGS frame but did not receive a timely response.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the SETTINGS_TIMEOUT error code, whose value is 0x04.
requirements.why_checkable: A timeout test can verify the selected error code and its numeric value.

requirements.quote:
STREAM_CLOSED (0x05):  The endpoint received a frame after a stream
      was half-closed.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame after a stream was half-closed.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the STREAM_CLOSED error code, whose value is 0x05.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame can be injected after the half-closed transition and the resulting error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
FRAME_SIZE_ERROR (0x06):  The endpoint received a frame with an
      invalid size.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame with an invalid size.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the FRAME_SIZE_ERROR error code, whose value is 0x06.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed frame sizes can be supplied and the selected error code verified.

requirements.quote:
REFUSED_STREAM (0x07):  The endpoint refused the stream prior to
      performing any application processing (see Section 8.7 for
      details).
requirements.condition: When an endpoint refuses a stream before performing any application processing.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the REFUSED_STREAM error code, whose value is 0x07.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can verify both that no application processing occurred and that the encoded error is 0x07.

requirements.quote:
CANCEL (0x08):  The endpoint uses this error code to indicate that
      the stream is no longer needed.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint indicates that a stream is no longer needed.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the CANCEL error code, whose value is 0x08.
requirements.why_checkable: The error code emitted for cancellation can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
COMPRESSION_ERROR (0x09):  The endpoint is unable to maintain the
      field section compression context for the connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint is unable to maintain the field section compression context for the connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the COMPRESSION_ERROR error code, whose value is 0x09.
requirements.why_checkable: Compression-context failure can be induced and the resulting error code checked.

requirements.quote:
CONNECT_ERROR (0x0a):  The connection established in response to a
      CONNECT request (Section 8.5) was reset or abnormally closed.
requirements.condition: When a connection established in response to a CONNECT request is reset or abnormally closed.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the CONNECT_ERROR error code, whose value is 0x0a.
requirements.why_checkable: Reset or abnormal closure of a CONNECT-established connection can be tested and the code inspected.

requirements.quote:
ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (0x0b):  The endpoint detected that its peer is
      exhibiting a behavior that might be generating excessive load.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint detects peer behavior that might be generating excessive load.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM error code, whose value is 0x0b.
requirements.why_checkable: When the implementation diagnoses this condition, its selected and encoded error code can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
INADEQUATE_SECURITY (0x0c):  The underlying transport has properties
      that do not meet minimum security requirements (see Section 9.2).
requirements.condition: When the underlying transport's properties do not meet minimum security requirements.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the INADEQUATE_SECURITY error code, whose value is 0x0c.
requirements.why_checkable: A transport with rejected security properties can be used to verify the emitted error code.

requirements.quote:
HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED (0x0d):  The endpoint requires that HTTP/1.1 be
      used instead of HTTP/2.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint requires HTTP/1.1 instead of HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED error code, whose value is 0x0d.
requirements.why_checkable: The error code used to demand protocol fallback can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
Unknown or unsupported error codes MUST NOT trigger any special
   behavior.  These MAY be treated by an implementation as being
   equivalent to INTERNAL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an unknown or unsupported error code is received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not trigger behavior specific to that unknown or unsupported code.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply unrecognized error-code values and observe whether code-specific behavior occurs.

requirements.quote:
Unknown or unsupported error codes MUST NOT trigger any special
   behavior.  These MAY be treated by an implementation as being
   equivalent to INTERNAL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an unknown or unsupported error code is received.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation may treat it as equivalent to INTERNAL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's handling path for an unrecognized code can be compared with its INTERNAL_ERROR path.

requirements.quote:
A client sends an HTTP request on a new stream, using a previously
   unused stream identifier (Section 5.1.1).  A server sends an HTTP
   response on the same stream as the request.
requirements.condition: When a client sends an HTTP request.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the request on a new stream using a previously unused stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initiate the request on an already-used stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream allocation history and the identifier used for each new request can be observed.

requirements.quote:
A client sends an HTTP request on a new stream, using a previously
   unused stream identifier (Section 5.1.1).  A server sends an HTTP
   response on the same stream as the request.
requirements.condition: When a server sends an HTTP response.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the response on the same stream as its request.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the response on a different stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Request and response stream identifiers can be correlated on the wire.

requirements.quote:
1.  one HEADERS frame (followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames)
       containing the header section (see Section 6.3 of [HTTP]),
requirements.condition: For an HTTP request or response message.
requirements.required_behavior: Begin the message with exactly one HEADERS frame containing the header section, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial frame type, count, content role, and continuation sequence can be parsed from a message.

requirements.quote:
2.  zero or more DATA frames containing the message content (see
       Section 6.4 of [HTTP]), and
requirements.condition: When an HTTP request or response has message content.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the message content in zero or more DATA frames after the initial header section.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame-sequence parser can verify the number, placement, and role of DATA frames.

requirements.quote:
3.  optionally, one HEADERS frame (followed by zero or more
       CONTINUATION frames) containing the trailer section, if present
       (see Section 6.5 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: When an HTTP request or response contains a trailer section.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the trailer section with one HEADERS frame followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include more than one trailer HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The trailer field-block sequence and number of trailer HEADERS frames can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
For a response only, a server MAY send any number of interim
   responses before the HEADERS frame containing a final response.  An
   interim response consists of a HEADERS frame (which might be followed
   by zero or more CONTINUATION frames) containing the control data and
   header section of an interim (1xx) HTTP response (see Section 15 of
   [HTTP]).  A HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set that carries
   an informational status code is malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When a server sends interim responses.
requirements.required_behavior: Send zero or more interim responses before the HEADERS frame containing the final response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send an interim response after the final response HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering of interim and final response HEADERS frames can be checked from the frame trace.

requirements.quote:
For a response only, a server MAY send any number of interim
   responses before the HEADERS frame containing a final response.  An
   interim response consists of a HEADERS frame (which might be followed
   by zero or more CONTINUATION frames) containing the control data and
   header section of an interim (1xx) HTTP response (see Section 15 of
   [HTTP]).  A HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set that carries
   an informational status code is malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: For an interim HTTP response.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a HEADERS frame containing the interim 1xx control data and header section, optionally followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The status code, field-block contents, and frame sequence of an interim response can be parsed.

requirements.quote:
For a response only, a server MAY send any number of interim
   responses before the HEADERS frame containing a final response.  An
   interim response consists of a HEADERS frame (which might be followed
   by zero or more CONTINUATION frames) containing the control data and
   header section of an interim (1xx) HTTP response (see Section 15 of
   [HTTP]).  A HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set that carries
   an informational status code is malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame carries an informational status code and has END_STREAM set.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted informational HEADERS frame with END_STREAM can verify malformed-message handling.

requirements.quote:
The last frame in the sequence bears an END_STREAM flag, noting that
   a HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set can be followed by
   CONTINUATION frames that carry any remaining fragments of the field
   block.
requirements.condition: At the end of an HTTP message's frame sequence.
requirements.required_behavior: Set END_STREAM on the frame that terminates the sequence; if that frame is HEADERS, allow following CONTINUATION frames only to finish that field block.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame flags and any field-block continuation frames are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
Other frames (from any stream) MUST NOT occur between the HEADERS
   frame and any CONTINUATION frames that might follow.
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame is followed by CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interleave any other frame, including a frame from another stream, between the HEADERS frame and its CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection-wide frame trace can detect any intervening frame.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 uses DATA frames to carry message content.  The chunked
   transfer encoding defined in Section 7.1 of [HTTP/1.1] cannot be used
   in HTTP/2; see Section 8.2.2.
requirements.condition: When carrying message content in HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: Use DATA frames to carry message content.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame types carrying message content can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 uses DATA frames to carry message content.  The chunked
   transfer encoding defined in Section 7.1 of [HTTP/1.1] cannot be used
   in HTTP/2; see Section 8.2.2.
requirements.condition: For an HTTP/2 message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoded messages can be inspected for chunked transfer-coding syntax or signaling.

requirements.quote:
Trailer fields are carried in a field block that also terminates the
   stream.  That is, trailer fields comprise a sequence starting with a
   HEADERS frame, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames, where
   the HEADERS frame bears an END_STREAM flag.  Trailers MUST NOT
   include pseudo-header fields (Section 8.3).  An endpoint that
   receives pseudo-header fields in trailers MUST treat the request or
   response as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When trailer fields are sent.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry them in a stream-terminating field block beginning with a HEADERS frame bearing END_STREAM and followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The trailer frame sequence and END_STREAM flag can be verified on the wire.

requirements.quote:
Trailer fields are carried in a field block that also terminates the
   stream.  That is, trailer fields comprise a sequence starting with a
   HEADERS frame, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames, where
   the HEADERS frame bears an END_STREAM flag.  Trailers MUST NOT
   include pseudo-header fields (Section 8.3).  An endpoint that
   receives pseudo-header fields in trailers MUST treat the request or
   response as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When constructing a trailer section.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include pseudo-header fields in trailers.
requirements.why_checkable: Decoded trailer fields can be inspected for pseudo-header names.

requirements.quote:
Trailer fields are carried in a field block that also terminates the
   stream.  That is, trailer fields comprise a sequence starting with a
   HEADERS frame, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames, where
   the HEADERS frame bears an END_STREAM flag.  Trailers MUST NOT
   include pseudo-header fields (Section 8.3).  An endpoint that
   receives pseudo-header fields in trailers MUST treat the request or
   response as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives pseudo-header fields in trailers.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the corresponding request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A trailer containing a pseudo-header can be injected and the endpoint's malformed-message response observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives a HEADERS frame without the END_STREAM flag
   set after receiving the HEADERS frame that opens a request or after
   receiving a final (non-informational) status code MUST treat the
   corresponding request or response as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a HEADERS frame without END_STREAM after the HEADERS frame that opened a request.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the corresponding request as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A second non-terminating HEADERS frame can be sent after request-opening headers and the result observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives a HEADERS frame without the END_STREAM flag
   set after receiving the HEADERS frame that opens a request or after
   receiving a final (non-informational) status code MUST treat the
   corresponding request or response as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a HEADERS frame without END_STREAM after receiving a final non-informational status code.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the corresponding response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-terminating HEADERS frame can be sent after final response headers and malformed handling verified.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP request/response exchange fully consumes a single stream.  A
   request starts with the HEADERS frame that puts the stream into the
   "open" state.  The request ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag
   set, which causes the stream to become "half-closed (local)" for the
   client and "half-closed (remote)" for the server.  A response stream
   starts with zero or more interim responses in HEADERS frames,
   followed by a HEADERS frame containing a final status code.
requirements.condition: For an HTTP request/response exchange.
requirements.required_behavior: Consume a single stream for the entire exchange.
requirements.why_checkable: All request and response frames can be checked for one common stream identifier.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP request/response exchange fully consumes a single stream.  A
   request starts with the HEADERS frame that puts the stream into the
   "open" state.  The request ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag
   set, which causes the stream to become "half-closed (local)" for the
   client and "half-closed (remote)" for the server.  A response stream
   starts with zero or more interim responses in HEADERS frames,
   followed by a HEADERS frame containing a final status code.
requirements.condition: When a request begins.
requirements.required_behavior: Begin it with a HEADERS frame that puts the stream into the open state.
requirements.why_checkable: The first request frame and resulting stream state can be observed.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP request/response exchange fully consumes a single stream.  A
   request starts with the HEADERS frame that puts the stream into the
   "open" state.  The request ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag
   set, which causes the stream to become "half-closed (local)" for the
   client and "half-closed (remote)" for the server.  A response stream
   starts with zero or more interim responses in HEADERS frames,
   followed by a HEADERS frame containing a final status code.
requirements.condition: When the request-ending frame with END_STREAM is sent or received.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to half-closed (local) for the client and half-closed (remote) for the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint roles, END_STREAM event, and subsequent stream states can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP request/response exchange fully consumes a single stream.  A
   request starts with the HEADERS frame that puts the stream into the
   "open" state.  The request ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag
   set, which causes the stream to become "half-closed (local)" for the
   client and "half-closed (remote)" for the server.  A response stream
   starts with zero or more interim responses in HEADERS frames,
   followed by a HEADERS frame containing a final status code.
requirements.condition: When forming a response stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Start with zero or more interim responses in HEADERS frames, followed by a HEADERS frame containing a final status code.
requirements.why_checkable: The response's HEADERS sequence and status codes can be parsed and ordered.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP response is complete after the server sends -- or the client
   receives -- a frame with the END_STREAM flag set (including any
   CONTINUATION frames needed to complete a field block).  A server can
   send a complete response prior to the client sending an entire
   request if the response does not depend on any portion of the request
   that has not been sent and received.  When this is true, a server MAY
   request that the client abort transmission of a request without error
   by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending
   a complete response (i.e., a frame with the END_STREAM flag set).
   Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a
   RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their
   discretion for other reasons.
requirements.condition: When the server sends or the client receives a frame with END_STREAM, after any CONTINUATION frames needed to finish its field block.
requirements.required_behavior: Regard the HTTP response as complete.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's completion event can be correlated with END_STREAM and field-block completion.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP response is complete after the server sends -- or the client
   receives -- a frame with the END_STREAM flag set (including any
   CONTINUATION frames needed to complete a field block).  A server can
   send a complete response prior to the client sending an entire
   request if the response does not depend on any portion of the request
   that has not been sent and received.  When this is true, a server MAY
   request that the client abort transmission of a request without error
   by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending
   a complete response (i.e., a frame with the END_STREAM flag set).
   Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a
   RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their
   discretion for other reasons.
requirements.condition: When a response does not depend on any unsent or unreceived portion of the request.
requirements.required_behavior: The server may send the complete response before the client has sent the entire request.
requirements.why_checkable: Request progress, response dependencies, and response timing can be controlled and observed.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP response is complete after the server sends -- or the client
   receives -- a frame with the END_STREAM flag set (including any
   CONTINUATION frames needed to complete a field block).  A server can
   send a complete response prior to the client sending an entire
   request if the response does not depend on any portion of the request
   that has not been sent and received.  When this is true, a server MAY
   request that the client abort transmission of a request without error
   by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending
   a complete response (i.e., a frame with the END_STREAM flag set).
   Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a
   RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their
   discretion for other reasons.
requirements.condition: After the server has sent a complete response that does not depend on an unsent or unreceived part of the request.
requirements.required_behavior: The server may request that the client abort request transmission by sending RST_STREAM with error code NO_ERROR after the complete response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send this abort-requesting RST_STREAM before sending the complete response.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame trace can verify the RST_STREAM code and its ordering after the response's END_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
An HTTP response is complete after the server sends -- or the client
   receives -- a frame with the END_STREAM flag set (including any
   CONTINUATION frames needed to complete a field block).  A server can
   send a complete response prior to the client sending an entire
   request if the response does not depend on any portion of the request
   that has not been sent and received.  When this is true, a server MAY
   request that the client abort transmission of a request without error
   by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending
   a complete response (i.e., a frame with the END_STREAM flag set).
   Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a
   RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their
   discretion for other reasons.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a NO_ERROR RST_STREAM sent after a complete response to request abortion.
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve and process the response unless it is discarded for another discretionary reason.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the response merely because that RST_STREAM was received.
requirements.why_checkable: A complete response followed by NO_ERROR RST_STREAM can be delivered and client retention behavior observed.

requirements.quote:
A malformed request or response is one that is an otherwise valid
   sequence of HTTP/2 frames but is invalid due to the presence of
   extraneous frames, prohibited fields or pseudo-header fields, the
   absence of mandatory pseudo-header fields, the inclusion of uppercase
   field names, or invalid field names and/or values (in certain
   circumstances; see Section 8.2).
requirements.condition: When an otherwise valid HTTP/2 frame sequence contains extraneous frames.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: An extraneous frame can be inserted into an otherwise valid sequence and classification observed.

requirements.quote:
A malformed request or response is one that is an otherwise valid
   sequence of HTTP/2 frames but is invalid due to the presence of
   extraneous frames, prohibited fields or pseudo-header fields, the
   absence of mandatory pseudo-header fields, the inclusion of uppercase
   field names, or invalid field names and/or values (in certain
   circumstances; see Section 8.2).
requirements.condition: When an otherwise valid HTTP/2 frame sequence contains a prohibited field or pseudo-header field.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A prohibited field can be injected and malformed-message classification observed.

requirements.quote:
A malformed request or response is one that is an otherwise valid
   sequence of HTTP/2 frames but is invalid due to the presence of
   extraneous frames, prohibited fields or pseudo-header fields, the
   absence of mandatory pseudo-header fields, the inclusion of uppercase
   field names, or invalid field names and/or values (in certain
   circumstances; see Section 8.2).
requirements.condition: When an otherwise valid HTTP/2 frame sequence omits a mandatory pseudo-header field.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Each mandatory pseudo-header can be omitted in a test and the classification observed.

requirements.quote:
A malformed request or response is one that is an otherwise valid
   sequence of HTTP/2 frames but is invalid due to the presence of
   extraneous frames, prohibited fields or pseudo-header fields, the
   absence of mandatory pseudo-header fields, the inclusion of uppercase
   field names, or invalid field names and/or values (in certain
   circumstances; see Section 8.2).
requirements.condition: When an otherwise valid HTTP/2 frame sequence includes an uppercase field name.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A field name containing uppercase characters can be supplied and classification observed.

requirements.quote:
A malformed request or response is one that is an otherwise valid
   sequence of HTTP/2 frames but is invalid due to the presence of
   extraneous frames, prohibited fields or pseudo-header fields, the
   absence of mandatory pseudo-header fields, the inclusion of uppercase
   field names, or invalid field names and/or values (in certain
   circumstances; see Section 8.2).
requirements.condition: When an otherwise valid HTTP/2 frame sequence contains an invalid field name or value in circumstances where it is prohibited.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Invalid field names and values can be supplied in applicable contexts and malformed classification observed.
